newsitem.title: USA: Republic, ADT call off merger.
newsitem.headline: Republic, ADT call off merger.

text.p: Republic Industries Inc. and ADT Ltd said Monday they agreed to terminate a proposed $5 billion merger of the two home and commercial security alarm companies.
The value of the stock transaction, originally pegged at $5 billion, has declined sharply since it was announced in July.

"Despite both companies' initial enthusiasm about this transaction, we now have agreed that this combination is no longer in the best interests of our respective companies," Republic Chairman Wayne Huizenga said in a statement.
Both companies said the pact's cancellation will enable them to pursue other opportunities.

"The delay in completing the transaction forced both companies to put business expansion plans on hold for too long. Both companies will now be free to resume their individual business plans," said Michael Ashcroft, chairman of ADT.

ADT is the largest electronic security company in North America and Britain. Its stock fell $1 to $18.875 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Republic's stock was up $1.6875 at $28.9375 on Nasdaq.

The companies had been haggling over revising the terms of the controversial transaction. Sources speculated that Ashcroft was seeking new terms in order to protect ADT shareholders against volatility in Republic stock.
In addition to the stock volatility, the transaction had faced opposition from Western Resources Inc., which holds a 24.3 percent stake in ADT.
Republic had insisted that the transaction would proceed and close by the end of the year. Shareholder proxies were expected to mailed out in the next couple of weeks.

The transaction had been viewed as a major step for Republic, which has bought 19 security companies since entering the market nearly a year ago. Its other two major areas of business are solid waste and used cars.
